Apple___Apple_scab: Collect fallen apple leaves after leaf drop. Prune crowded branches so foliage dries sooner, and choose scab-resistant varieties for new trees.
Apple___Black_rot: Remove mummified apples and dead or cankered wood during dry weather. Check branches for cankers as well as fruit symptoms.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust: Look for orange rust spots and nearby junipers with galls. Choose rust-resistant apple varieties for new plantings and ask a local fruit specialist about protecting new growth.
Apple___healthy: Continue routine care and inspect new leaves regularly. If other parts of the plant show symptoms, photograph those separately before choosing a treatment.
Blueberry___healthy: Continue routine care and inspect new leaves regularly. If other parts of the plant show symptoms, photograph those separately before choosing a treatment.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew: Prune crowded cherry shoots to improve airflow. Check young leaves for fresh powdery patches and consult a fruit specialist if new growth continues to be affected.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy: Continue routine care and inspect new leaves regularly. If other parts of the plant show symptoms, photograph those separately before choosing a treatment.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray: Choose a gray leaf spot-resistant hybrid for the next planting. Rotate with a non-corn crop where practical and monitor leaves around the ear during the season.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_: Check both leaf surfaces for rust pustules. Use a resistant hybrid in future plantings and get the rust type confirmed before deciding on treatment.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight: Use a resistant hybrid and rotate away from corn where practical. Monitor lesion spread toward the ear leaves and seek local advice if symptoms appear early.
Corn_(maize)___healthy: Continue routine care and inspect new leaves regularly. If other parts of the plant show symptoms, photograph those separately before choosing a treatment.
Grape___Black_rot: Remove shriveled grape berries from the canopy and ground. Prune for airflow and protect new fruit according to local vineyard guidance.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles): Mark the affected vine and ask a viticulture specialist to examine the trunk. Esca affects woody tissue and a leaf spray cannot restore damaged wood.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo: Thin a crowded canopy and remove fallen infected foliage. Have the spots identified before choosing any crop protection product.
Grape___healthy: Continue routine care and inspect new leaves regularly. If other parts of the plant show symptoms, photograph those separately before choosing a treatment.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening): Contact your local plant-health service for confirmation. Citrus greening has no cure. Avoid moving citrus plants or cuttings while awaiting advice.
Peach___Bacterial_spot: Select a bacterial spot-resistant peach variety for new plantings. Reduce leaf wetness and ask a local orchard specialist about protecting new growth.
Peach___healthy: Continue routine care and inspect new leaves regularly. If other parts of the plant show symptoms, photograph those separately before choosing a treatment.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot: Use clean pepper transplants, water at soil level, and avoid handling wet plants. Rotate the bed away from peppers and tomatoes.
Pepper,_bell___healthy: Continue routine care and inspect new leaves regularly. If other parts of the plant show symptoms, photograph those separately before choosing a treatment.
Potato___Early_blight: Remove volunteer potatoes and old crop debris. Rotate away from potatoes and tomatoes and monitor lower leaves for expanding spots.
Potato___Late_blight: Seek prompt confirmation from a local crop adviser. Avoid moving suspect tubers or foliage and use certified seed potatoes for the next crop.
Potato___healthy: Continue routine care and inspect new leaves regularly. If other parts of the plant show symptoms, photograph those separately before choosing a treatment.

Soybean___healthy: Continue routine care and inspect new leaves regularly. If other parts of the plant show symptoms, photograph those separately before choosing a treatment.
Squash___Powdery_mildew: Improve spacing around vines and inspect both leaf surfaces. For future plantings, choose squash varieties with powdery mildew resistance.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch: Remove old affected strawberry leaves and improve airflow through crowded rows. Water at ground level and use healthy planting stock.
Strawberry___healthy: Continue routine care and inspect new leaves regularly. If other parts of the plant show symptoms, photograph those separately before choosing a treatment.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot: Use disease-free tomato transplants and avoid working among wet plants. Water at the base and rotate the bed away from tomatoes and peppers.
Tomato___Early_blight: Remove badly spotted lower leaves, mulch to limit soil splash, and support plants above the ground. Rotate the planting site next season.
Tomato___Late_blight: Get rapidly spreading lesions confirmed promptly by a local plant clinic. Avoid moving suspect plants and follow local guidance for disposal.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold: Increase ventilation, especially in greenhouses. Space and prune plants to reduce humidity and remove heavily affected leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot: Remove spotted lower leaves, mulch the soil, and irrigate at the base. Clean up old tomato foliage at the end of the season.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider: Check leaf undersides with a hand lens for moving mites or webbing. Rinse small infestations from leaf undersides with water and inspect again for live mites.
Tomato___Target_Spot: Improve airflow and reduce splash irrigation. Remove infected debris after harvest and confirm the diagnosis because several tomato leaf spots look similar.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus: Inspect new growth and leaf undersides for whiteflies. Have the virus confirmed, remove confirmed infected plants, and use healthy transplants and resistant varieties.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus: Have mosaic symptoms confirmed. Remove confirmed infected plants, clean tools between plants, and use clean seed or transplants.
Tomato___healthy: Continue routine care and inspect new leaves regularly. If other parts of the plant show symptoms, photograph those separately before choosing a treatment.
